quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
rationale: Section 8 contains a one-way vendor indemnity in our favour: Commerce One must indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers against third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with a standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control to the vendor at its expense and counsel, cooperation at vendor's cost, plus a right for us to join with our own counsel). Exclusions are narrow and conventional (use other than as set out in the Documentation; modification by a party other than Commerce One where the infringement would not otherwise have occurred), and the remedy ladder is the usual procure / replace or modify / terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid. Section 9 expressly carves Section 8 out of both the 12-month fees cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so the indemnity is uncapped — better for us than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. There is no Corio-side indemnity anywhere in the agreement, so the "narrow Customer indemnity" limb is satisfied by omission. The clause therefore meets the fallback (indeed exceeds it on the cap) and is compliant; no redline. Noted for the record only as sub-element gaps short of the preferred position: the indemnity does not extend to vendor breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data caused by the vendor, or vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the refund is tied to fees "paid" rather than "paid or payable". Given the uncapped IP indemnity and the absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us, these are not worth negotiating capital.

No deterministic check failures and no over-reach: nothing was flagged that benefits our party, and no negotiation issue is raised.

quote: 2. Corio Customer Application Management Revenue: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
rationale:
This meets the preferred position: the agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, or volume commitment on Corio. Our payment obligations are limited to (i) the one-time BuySite license fee due on Software Acceptance, (ii) annual maintenance/support and MarketSite.net access fees for services actually made available, and (iii) a revenue share calculated on actual Application Management Revenue received from Corio Customers — i.e., pure pass-through of realized usage, with no floor, no guaranteed minimum, and no shortfall penalty. Exhibit B expressly sets Software Users at "Unlimited," so there is no volume cap on our usage either.

Three points noted but not flagged. First, the "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" in Exhibit B (p0158) is a qualifying threshold on the revenue-share *exemption* for the initial 3000 licenses, not a purchase commitment or seat minimum we must buy or pay for. Second, the five-year initial term (Section 11.1) with no termination-for-convenience right is a term-length point rather than a minimum-volume commitment, and Section 4.2 makes maintenance continuation expressly conditional on Corio electing to "continue to pay" the annual fees, which gives us a practical exit from the recurring spend. Third, Exhibit D's sales and marketing items — including the two-customer order target — are stated as "non-binding" and qualified by "commercially reasonable efforts," so they create no enforceable volume obligation. The shortfall reference in Section 4.4 concerns audit true-up of amounts payable and is mutual ("the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment"), which is the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers rather than a penalty. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape for a compliant finding. The cited paragraphs support the conclusion: fees are limited to a one-time license fee (4.1), annual maintenance fees that continue only if Corio elects to keep paying (4.2), and a revenue share computed on actual Application Management Revenue received (p0157) — no floor, guaranteed minimum, or shortfall penalty on the Customer. Exhibit B shows Software Users as 'Unlimited' (p0151), so there is no volume cap on our usage; the '40 Authorized Software Users per Customer' language in p0158 is correctly read as a qualifying threshold for the revenue-share exemption rather than a purchase obligation. ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, and in addition to its surviving obligations under Section 11.3, Commerce One shall: (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers for a period of up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's written request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers then in Commerce One's possession or control, including all data generated through or stored in the MarketSite.net Service, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing, except to the extent retention is required to perform Commerce One's surviving obligations under this Agreement or by applicable law.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 11.4 requiring post-termination transition assistance (up to 6 months at then-current rates) and return of Corio/Customer data within 30 days in machine-readable format, followed by deletion and written certification.

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Section 11.3 gives us useful run-off rights (continued Customer access under Section 2, surviving support and maintenance, plus the Section 12 source code escrow), but the Agreement contains no post-termination transition-assistance right and no data return/export obligation. The only exit mechanic is a mutual "return or destroy" of Confidential Information at the disclosing party's option, with no format, no timescale and no deletion certification, which does not reach even the fallback (90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days). Because Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service through which our Customers transact, our and our Customers' data can sit on its systems with no contractual route back to us. We therefore insert a new Section 11.4 at the preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, and deletion with written certification thereafter, carved back for Commerce One's surviving obligations and legal retention so the new clause does not cut across the Section 11.3 run-off.

quote: 14.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.

However, it falls short of the fallback on a material term: consent for all other assignments is left to the other party's absolute discretion, with no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, and there is no affiliate carve-out, so a routine internal reorganization by Corio could be blocked outright. The proposed edit is the minimum needed — it adds the reasonableness standard and an affiliate carve-out while preserving the existing mutual structure. The remaining gaps against the preferred position (the direct-competitor consent carve-back applies to Corio's transactions as well as Commerce One's, rather than only barring assignment to a Corio competitor) are noted but not pressed, given the balanced mutual bargain struck in this clause.
